# Edits automation server

Edits for Mac can run a local MCP server that lets an agent build and export edits with
Edits' own tools, the same ones the user sees. Hosts rename the tools: Claude Code shows
`mcp__metapilot-native__importMedia`, and Voyager's integrations shorten and hash the name.
Recognise them by the Edits name inside, and read the arguments the session lists rather
than assuming them from this file.

## Setup

The user does this once, in Edits: **Settings → Automation → Enable Automation Server**.
That page shows the port and the **Access token**. Anyone with the token can edit their
projects while the server is on, so never ask for it in the chat, and never repeat it or
write it to a file. When a tool error asks you to have the user paste the token, give them
these steps instead. Then connect it one of two ways:

- **Through Voyager:** Apps & Models → Apps → **Instagram Edits** → paste the token and
  choose **Connect**. Voyager saves it with the token kept private and checks it. If the
  user would rather add it by hand, use **Add an app or service** → **Add a tool server by
  its address**, name it Instagram Edits, give the address `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`
  with the port Edits shows, and under **More options** set **Sign-in** to **Access token**.
- **Through Claude Code or Codex:** under **Connect an AI client**, Edits shows a command
  for each. The user runs it in Terminal, then turns the server on in Apps & Models →
  **Providers** → **Claude** or **ChatGPT** → **Advanced** → **Bring in from Claude Code**
  or **Bring in from Codex** → **Tool servers**. New servers start off.

Tools arrive with the next conversation, not the current one. Don't edit the user's
harness configuration yourself. The server only answers while Edits is open with the
setting on. If the user regenerates the token, calls fail with an authentication error
until they paste the new token into the connection they set up.

## Working

- Start with `appState`. Which tools work depends on the screen: open or create a project
  (`projects`, `openProject`, `newProject`) before editing, and call `getCapabilities`
  when unsure. Edits can return to its home screen during a long run. When a tool says
  it isn't available on this screen, check `appState`, reopen the project and carry on.
  Element IDs survive the reopen.
- Paths are absolute. Edits can read `~/Movies` once the user has let it use that folder,
  which it asks on first launch. If an import fails with "Sandbox bookmark unavailable",
  copy the file into `~/Library/Containers/com.burbn.basel.mac/Data/tmp/` and import it
  from there instead. macOS may ask the user to let Voyager reach another app's data.
  Symbolic links are refused, so copy, don't link.
- `importMedia` adds a video or image to the project and puts it on the timeline in one
  step. `addMedia` is for audio only and needs `audioKind`: `music`, `soundEffect` or
  `voiceover`. `setCanvas` (`aspect` `9:16`, `frameRate` 24, 30 or 60) sets the frame.
- For captions in the user's own style, run `generateCaptions`, then `listCaptionStyles`
  and `setCaptionStyle`.
- Check your work with frames, not screenshots of the window: `captureFrame` for one
  moment, or `previewVideo` and then `previewVideoFrames` for a range.
- `saveProject` before handing back, so the user finds the project in Edits.

## Export

Call `setExportSettings` with `resolutionType`, `aspectRatio`, `quality`, `dynamicRange`
and `frameRate` together. The values are `resolutionType` `720p`, `HD`, `2K` or `4K` (`HD`
is 1080 wide for a reel), `aspectRatio` `nineBySixteen`, `sixteenByNine`, `fourByFive`,
`oneByOne` and so on, `quality` `Low`, `Med` or `High`, and `dynamicRange` `SDR` or `HDR`.
If one is missing, `export` fails with "incomplete preset row". Then call
`export` with an absolute output path under `~/Movies/Voyager/<project>/`, and poll
`exportStatus` until it finishes. Check the file with `voyager media review FILE --json`
before calling it done, because the frame rate Edits writes can differ from the one
requested.

# Posting from Edits

The automation server can't post. Posting goes through Edits' **Share to Instagram** screen
with [computer-use](../../computer-use/SKILL.md), as the account signed in to Edits. A post
is public and can't be quietly taken back, so post only when the user has asked you to.

Before opening the share screen:

- Run `voyager media review FILE --platform reels --json` on the export and fix what
  it flags (see [publish-video](../../publish-video/SKILL.md#establish-the-release)).
- Settle every choice with the user in one message: the caption, the cover frame,
  **Audience** (Everyone, Followers or Close friends), **Also share to Feed**, location,
  people to tag, and whether it's a **Trial reel** (shown to non-followers first, with
  **Manual** or **Automatic** sharing to followers afterwards). Keep the account's usual
  settings for anything they leave open, and say which ones you kept.
- Turn on **Add AI Label** when the picture or voice is AI-generated and looks real.
  Instagram requires it, and may add the label itself when it detects AI. Ask the user
  when you aren't sure.
- Edits may offer Meta AI voice translation. Accepting it agrees to Meta's AI terms on the
  user's behalf, so leave it off unless the user turned it on themselves.

Then, in the open project, enter what the user approved, compare the whole screen against
it, and choose **Share** once. Edits shows its progress ("Uploading video...", "Waiting
for processing...") and ends with **Shared successfully.** or **Share failed**. On success,
open **View on Instagram** and record the reel's address. On failure, or when you can't
tell what happened, don't share again until you've checked the account's profile for the
reel: a share that looked like it failed may still have gone through.

Keep a receipt in `publishing/instagram/receipts.json`, as described in
[publish-video](../../publish-video/SKILL.md#submit-once-and-reconcile).

## Cards in the chat

Voyager draws four cards from a fenced block with the language `voyager-edits-card` and one
line of JSON. Write the block on its own, after a sentence that says what it is for:

- ` {"card":"connect"} ` when Edits isn't connected: its **Set up** button opens the Edits
  sheet in Apps & Models.
- ` {"card":"share","account":"@name","video":"1080x1920, 0:42","caption":"...","cover":"Frame
  at 0:03","audience":"Everyone · also in Feed","trialReel":"Off","aiLabel":"On · AI
  voice-over"} ` once every choice above is settled, instead of asking in prose. **Post reel**
  answers "Post the reel." and **Change something** answers "I want to change something
  before you post." Post only after **Post reel**.
- ` {"card":"sharing","status":"Uploading video..."} ` while the Share screen is working.
  **Stop** stops the turn.
- ` {"card":"shared","url":"https://www.instagram.com/reel/..."} ` when Edits reports success
  and you have the address. Leave `url` out when you don't.

---
name: instagram-edits
description: "."
applications:
  - id: instagram-edits
    role: primary
---

Edits is Instagram's video editor. On a Mac it can finish a short-form video and post it
to Instagram as a reel. It runs on Apple silicon Macs (macOS 15.1 or later) and needs the
user signed in with their Instagram account. There is no Windows or Intel version: on those
computers, use [publish-video](../publish-video/references/instagram.md) to post the file.

Ask first, unless the request already answers it:

- Should Edits only receive the finished cut, or should you also post it to Instagram?

Know:

- Cut, voice and caption the piece with [edit-video](../edit-video/SKILL.md) first, so Edits
  only adds finishing touches. Edits makes its own captions with `generateCaptions`; don't
  burn in Voyager captions as well.
- Edits is sandboxed and can't open files from most folders. Put everything it needs in
  `~/Movies/Voyager/<project>/`, which it can read and write. Make the folder with the shell.
- Edits projects live in Edits' own library. Voyager can't write one. Bring work in by
  importing media, and take it out by exporting a file or posting.

## Which route

- **Automation server:** Edits tools are in this session (names such as `appState`,
  `importMedia` and `setExportSettings`, usually under a server named `metapilot-native`
  or `edits`, or shortened and hashed under Voyager's integrations). Read
  [automation](references/automation.md) for setup, editing and export.
- **No Edits tools:** read [automation](references/automation.md#setup) and give the user
  the steps. Until the tools arrive, copy the files into the folder above and ask the user
  to import them, or drive the window with [computer-use](../computer-use/SKILL.md).

The automation server has no posting tool. To post, read [posting](references/posting.md).
